entities.summary: Frederick of Blankenheim served as Bishop of Strasbourg from 1375 to 1393 and then as Bishop of Utrecht from 1393 until his death in 1423. His tenure as Bishop of Strasbourg was marked by his efforts to promote the Reformation and his involvement in the Council of Basel. As Bishop of Utrecht, he played a crucial role in the establishment of the city's cathedral and the development of the city's educational institutions. Frederick's legacy as a bishop and a theologian has been recognized by his inclusion in the canon of Catholic saints. His contributions to the religious and cultural landscape of Europe during the Late Middle Ages are still studied by historians today. The city of Utrecht, where he served as bishop, remains a testament to his enduring influence on the region's history and culture. Despite the challenges posed by the Black Death and the Hundred Years' War, Frederick's leadership and vision helped to shape the spiritual and intellectual life of the region. The legacy of Frederick of Blankenheim serves as a reminder of the importance of religious and cultural institutions in shaping the course of human history.
